title: Bound six paid-slot repairs and 73 linked chart cones on #7786
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

On the 1,289-coordinate rational word from #7786, six named pairs of chronological paid rows cannot replace `95914 → 88` with a single `278 → 127` rank-seven send under the stated preservation contract. The later row may observe the earlier edit through its actual causal stock. Each repair must preserve 387 exterior and 901 receiver observations. The exact witness separates the original terminal `155442 = 1` from the collapsed value `0`. Two controls realize nonzero compatible pair recodings before the collapse and still lose that terminal.

The standalone directed-price replay also closes the remaining 73 saved linked two-reversal cones with both reversals and all 400 physical main chart pairs fixed. A regeneration checks all 934 nominations, the 66 inherited price certificates, and the 73 new price certificates. The most favorable new directed saving upper is `−11.8737978602670848678835793786636822` across 48 rational calls, against a required saving of at least `0.379442169416081001142560448506083557440402716` at κ `0.00387981257853`. The scoped findings retain the incumbent conditional finite lower `0.00387944011068` and leave the supplier target open.

## Validation

From the package directory in standard-library CPython 3.12, run the sealed source and receipts.

```sh
python3.12 -IB verify_stock.py
python3.12 -IB cones/portable.py
```

The independent stock replay took about 8 CPU seconds with about 90 MiB peak RSS. The standalone cone replay used about 102 CPU seconds with about 245 MiB peak RSS. Both are network-free. The stock check includes omission, wrong-sign and concrete nonzero recoding controls. The cone check independently regenerates the roster, includes the zero-reversal source control, and rejects a perturbed integer-flow floor. Registered replay and a dedicated hosted workflow run the same two checks. The altered physical caller, dirty erasure, ordinary compiler and outer analysis remain obligations for a future surviving candidate.
